package_info.why_malicious: Attackers covertly inserted a sophisticated backdoor (SUNBURST) into the SolarWinds Orion software update process, resulting in a large-scale supply chain attack. The malicious code enabled persistent remote access, command execution, and data exfiltration from victim environments, impacting thousands of organizations globally.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (on service start or update install)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The code establishes a covert communication channel to attacker-controlled servers by initiating periodic outbound connections (beacons) from the Orion BusinessLayerHost process. Upon successful contact, it can receive and execute arbitrary commands, download and run additional payloads, exfiltrate sensitive data, and facilitate lateral movement within the network. The code is designed to evade detection by checking for debugging environments and delaying execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is surreptitiously embedded within a core Orion DLL and activates only under specific conditions to avoid detection. It initiates unauthorized outbound network connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure, unrelated to any legitimate SolarWinds operations. The ability to execute arbitrary remote commands and download further payloads is highly indicative of backdoor functionality.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate SolarWinds Orion software should not contain hidden code that establishes covert channels to external servers or executes remote instructions. Official updates must not introduce obfuscated, conditionally-activated backdoors into core DLLs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise management tools may connect to central servers for updates or telemetry, but such behavior is always documented, uses official domains, and never includes hidden command execution or obfuscation.
key_indicators: Obfuscated and conditionally-activated code within SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll
Outbound network connections from BusinessLayerHost to suspicious or unlisted domains
Execution of arbitrary commands received from remote servers
Checks for debugging or sandbox environments to evade analysis
Persistence via legitimate Orion service startup

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is covertly inserted into the SolarWinds Orion Core BusinessLayer DLL during the vendor's build process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Distribution of backdoored software to SolarWinds customers via official update channels

attack_chain.action: Customers install the compromised update, causing the malicious DLL to be loaded and executed within the Orion environment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Activation of the backdoor in customer environments

attack_chain.action: The backdoor code establishes outbound connections to attacker-controlled command and control (C2) servers, beacons for instructions, and awaits further commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote command execution, data exfiltration, and potential lateral movement within victim networks

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from the Orion BusinessLayerHost process to external domains
Presence of obfuscated or anomalous code within SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll
Conditional execution logic that delays or suppresses activity in debugging or sandbox environments
Orion processes spawning unexpected child processes or accessing sensitive files atypical for normal operation
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with a hash value not matching the official SolarWinds release
Presence of unknown or modified DLLs in the Orion software installation directory
Timestamp anomalies or digital signature mismatches in Orion DLLs
network_indicators: Outbound connections or DNS queries to known Sunburst C2 domains such as avsvmcloud.com, digitalcollege.org, and others listed in threat intelligence feeds
Unusual HTTP/S traffic patterns from Orion servers to external IPs/domains not associated with SolarWinds
Beaconing behavior with periodic intervals from Orion servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor for unexpected outbound network connections from SolarWinds Orion processes, especially to known Sunburst C2 domains and IPs. Validate the integrity of all Orion DLLs by comparing their hashes against official SolarWinds releases and checking for digital signature anomalies. Use endpoint detection and response (EDR) or antivirus tools to scan for obfuscated or suspicious code within Orion binaries. Monitor for process behaviors such as Orion services spawning unauthorized child processes or accessing files outside their normal scope. Correlate network, file, and process indicators to identify potential compromise.
